names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 22 Μαΐου, «Άγιοι Αιμίλιος και Κάστος οι Αφρικανοί», with «Άγιοι» left off; the life page's own head line for him reads «Αγιος Αιμιλιος ο Αφρικανος».

death.note: saint.gr: «Οι Άγιοι Μάρτυρες Κάστος και Αιμίλιος μαρτύρησαν το 251 μ.Χ. στην Καρχηδόνα επί Σεπτιμίου Σεβήρου.» The page's year and the reign it names do not agree, and neither is corrected here; the year is what it prints, and its head line repeats it as «(; - 251)».

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 22ας Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Αιμίλιος και Κάστος οι Αφρικανοί»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 22 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and carries both men under two head lines, so this is a company of two named men and therefore two folders. The corpus keeps no Aemilius of Africa: its `emilian-of-durostorum`, `emilian-of-trebia`, `emilian-the-confessor` and `emilia-mother-of-basil-the-great` are other people on other days. The page says the account of the martyrdom comes from Saint Cyprian and from Augustine; that is a citation and not an association, so no `related` row is made for either of them. No hymn, no relics.
